title: Noise stability and signed dictators
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<\rho<1$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be balanced, meaning that its mean under the uniform measure on the cube is zero. Form a correlated pair $(X,Y)$ by choosing $X$ uniformly and, independently in each coordinate, keeping its sign with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and flipping it otherwise. Then $\mathbb{E}[f(X)f(Y)]=\rho$ if and only if there is a coordinate $i$ such that $f(x)=x_i$ for every $x$, or $f(x)=-x_i$ for every $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$f$ has mean zero under the uniform measure
